Best known for creating and hosting groundbreaking television such as Good Eats, Iron Chef America, Cutthroat Kitchen, and Food Network Star, Brown has also built one of the most successful culinary touring franchises ever, performing live in more than 300 cities for well over half a million fans. With An Evening of Alton Brown, he strips away the spectacle in favor of connection, spontaneity, and storytelling, delivering a show that is equal part humor, science, food, and heart.

events.title: Civil War History in Oakton and Vienna
events.description: Greater Oakton Community Association invites history enthusiasts to join a narrated historic bus tour led by acclaimed local historian Jim Lewis on from 9:00 a.m. to 1:00 p.m. Please arrive at 9:00 a.m. at Oakton Community Park at 2841 Hunter Mill Road (next to the old schoolhouse and roundabout) for Jim Lewis's opening comments, then board the bus for departure by 9:30 a.m. The tour will end at 1:00 p.m. This 3.5-hour journey spans Fairfax County's history from its formation in 1742 through the early 1900s, focusing on sites primarily on or just off Hunter Mill Road. Participants hear stories of where the old mills and roads were located and learn about famed military figures (particularly from the Civil War era) and colorful residents who graced the area. Numerous period photographs support the narrative, bringing history to life. Walking requirements are minimal, although one segment involves going down a slight grassy decline. The tour runs rain or shine. Snacks and water are included. Cost is $45 per seat. In the event of cancellation, refunds are provided if a replacement is found for the seat; a wait list is maintained for this purpose. There are 23 seats on the bus. Special "Event Pricing" is offered for the award-winning "Danger Between the Lines" DVD and tour-related illustrated books, available for purchase with cash only. Narrated Historic Bus Tour with Jim Lewis combines local history education, community connection, and immersive storytelling in Fairfax County, Virginia. Questions? Email contact@greateroakton.com . events.description: Discover the fascinating world of superstitions, folklore, and everyday beliefs that shaped life in centuries past. Join us for an engaging journey into the beliefs that helped people make sense of an uncertain world and discover how echoes of these old superstitions still linger today. At the conclusion of the tour, guests are invited to enjoy seasonal refreshments and share their favorite superstition! Note: This tour will be offered on a range of dates and times in October. To see times, visit our October event calendar . Cost: $15 General Admission. $12 for Historic Annapolis members and Military. Weather or private events may alter the tour route. events.address: 11201 Bethesda Church Road, Damascus View, Diamond View
events.description: Welcome to L eech Woods According to Montgomery County historical land records, the present site of Leech Woods was originally settled by Warwick and Jeanne Leech and their six children sometime in early 1790. Having immigrated from Hungary, the family chose Damascus, Maryland, based on its temperate climate and heavily wooded region, which reminded them of their homeland. The Leech family store thrived as the leading local merchant of hides, furs, and hunting supplies. During the disastrous Winter of 1804, the Leech family store was robbed and vandalized by unknown attackers and the body of John Leech, the youngest son, was found nailed to the back wall of the store. The remaining bodies of the family members were later found bludgeoned and bound inside of the root cellar of their homestead. No further information about the attackers or motives for the killings is known. ​ Remnants of the Leech family homestead still stand deep in the woods where the present Leech Woods experience is built. The Leech Woods immersive experience follows the original walking path from the site of the Leech family hunting supply store to the remnants of the original family homestead. As the property was classified as a historical site in 1972, no artifacts may be removed, and we ask that you respect the privacy of the grave sites. What’s new? More Scares. More scenes. events.title: The Legend of Sleepy Hollow-Olney Theatre
events.description: Olney audiences were blown away in 2025, when we invited Synetic Theater to perform their award-winning, wordless version of Shakespeare’s A Midsummer Night’s Dream . Now they’re back, but this time they’re tackling a story with classic American roots in the intimate confines of Olney Theatre Center’s 150-seat Theatre Lab. In the haunted village of Sleepy Hollow, the past refuses to stay buried. Years after a brutal Revolutionary War encounter leaves a Hessian soldier beheaded and his beloved horse slain, the fallen rider returns as the legendary Headless Horseman—an apparition stalking the shadowed forests in search of what was taken from him. Inspired by Washington Irving’s classic tale, Sleepy Hollow reimagines the familiar legend as a haunting story of love, guilt, revenge, and redemption. Blending supernatural horror with theatrical spectacle, it asks whether the true monsters are the spirits who haunt us—or the deeds we would rather forget. By Washington Irving Adapted by Nathan Weinberger Directed by Paata Tsikurishvili Choreographed by Irina Tsikurishvili Due to the layout of the Mulitz-Gudelsky Theatre Lab, late seating is at the discretion of the House Manager. Those exiting the theatre during the performance will not be re-admitted while the performance is in progress.

events.title: Leech Woods
events.address: 11201 Bethesda Church Road, Damascus View, Diamond View
events.description: Welcome to L eech Woods According to Montgomery County historical land records, the present site of Leech Woods was originally settled by Warwick and Jeanne Leech and their six children sometime in early 1790. Having immigrated from Hungary, the family chose Damascus, Maryland, based on its temperate climate and heavily wooded region, which reminded them of their homeland. The Leech family store thrived as the leading local merchant of hides, furs, and hunting supplies. During the disastrous Winter of 1804, the Leech family store was robbed and vandalized by unknown attackers and the body of John Leech, the youngest son, was found nailed to the back wall of the store. The remaining bodies of the family members were later found bludgeoned and bound inside of the root cellar of their homestead. No further information about the attackers or motives for the killings is known. ​ Remnants of the Leech family homestead still stand deep in the woods where the present Leech Woods experience is built. The Leech Woods immersive experience follows the original walking path from the site of the Leech family hunting supply store to the remnants of the original family homestead. As the property was classified as a historical site in 1972, no artifacts may be removed, and we ask that you respect the privacy of the grave sites. What’s new? More Scares. More scenes. events.title: The Legend of Sleepy Hollow-Olney Theatre
events.description: Olney audiences were blown away in 2025, when we invited Synetic Theater to perform their award-winning, wordless version of Shakespeare’s A Midsummer Night’s Dream . Now they’re back, but this time they’re tackling a story with classic American roots in the intimate confines of Olney Theatre Center’s 150-seat Theatre Lab. In the haunted village of Sleepy Hollow, the past refuses to stay buried. Years after a brutal Revolutionary War encounter leaves a Hessian soldier beheaded and his beloved horse slain, the fallen rider returns as the legendary Headless Horseman—an apparition stalking the shadowed forests in search of what was taken from him. Inspired by Washington Irving’s classic tale, Sleepy Hollow reimagines the familiar legend as a haunting story of love, guilt, revenge, and redemption. Blending supernatural horror with theatrical spectacle, it asks whether the true monsters are the spirits who haunt us—or the deeds we would rather forget. By Washington Irving Adapted by Nathan Weinberger Directed by Paata Tsikurishvili Choreographed by Irina Tsikurishvili Due to the layout of the Mulitz-Gudelsky Theatre Lab, late seating is at the discretion of the House Manager. Those exiting the theatre during the performance will not be re-admitted while the performance is in progress.

events.title: An Evening with ACOUSTIC ALCHEMY – RESCHEDULED TO APRIL 6, 2027!
Annapolis Witches & Legends Walking Tour
events.description: Take a walk through the history of Maryland's witch trials, superstition, and local legends with Annapolis Ghost Tours. Between the 1600s and 1700s, Maryland saw at least twelve witch trials. The last one was a capital case held right here in Annapolis. Several women in the colony were killed under suspicion of witchcraft, one was legally executed, and the stories of others have become legends that persist to this day. On this 90-minute walking tour, we will talk about the superstitions and accusations through the lens of local history.

events.title: Crossing the Red Line: Biden, His Advisors, and Israel's War in Gaza
events.description: The Middle East Policy Forum will host award-winning foreign affairs journalist Akbar Shahid Ahmed, author of Crossing the Red Line: Biden, His Advisors, and Israel's War in Gaza, on Wednesday, October 28. In a discussion moderated by Professor Marc Lynch, Ahmed will offer his powerful and authoritative account of how the Biden administration fueled atrocities in Gaza. In vivid prose and with unparalleled access to insiders, Ahmed depicts a White House that resisted a course correction as its failures became undeniable. He probes Biden’s inner circle, whose choices fueled tens of thousands of avoidable deaths among Palestinians, Lebanese, and Israelis, torpedoed long-time standards for warfare, and created a more dangerous world for us all. The Biden administration’s decisions drove voter backlash that helped Donald Trump regain power, and established patterns of impunity that have spurred wider bloodshed under Trump. Crossing the Red Line is an urgent reckoning with Biden’s record on Gaza that is vital to understanding historic damage to America’s standing in the world, and a period whose dark consequences will resonate globally for decades to come. events.title: Hitchcocktober at the Angelika
events.description: Join us this October to celebrate Alfred Hitchcock, the master who gave us some of the most suspenseful moments in film history! STRANGERS ON A TRAIN October 7 at 4:00 and 7:00 Guy Haines wants a divorce. Bruno Antony wants his father dead. When the two meet aboard a train, Bruno proposes a solution to both their problems: he will murder Guy’s wife and Guy will murder Bruno’s father, leaving two victims and no motives. REAR WINDOW October 14 at 4:00 and 7:00 A newspaper photographer (James Stewart) with a broken leg passes time by observing his neighbors through his window. One evening, he sees what he believes to be a murder and decides to solve the crime himself, with the help of his nurse and his girlfriend (Grace Kelly). SUSPICION October 21 at 4:00 and 7:00 After eloping with a charming playboy (Cary Grant), Lina McLaidlaw (Joan Fontaine) soon discovers his gambling vice and mounting debts. As his lies deepen and those around him meet mysterious ends, Lina begins to suspect that her husband’s affection may conceal a deadly motive— and that she could be his next victim. VERTIGO October 28 at 4:00 and 7:00 Retired San Francisco police detective Scottie Ferguson (James Stewart) wrestles with his personal demons as he finds himself becoming obsessed with the beautiful woman (Kim Novak) he has been hired to trail, whose husband believes she is possessed. PSYCHO October 31 at 4:00 and 7:00 When Marion Crane (Janet Leigh) ends up at the Bates Motel after making off with $40,000 cash, there's hardly a film fan alive who doesn't know what happens next. It wouldn't be Hitchcocktober without his biggest hit!

events.title: SILENT FILM Series: The Cabinet of Dr. Caligari (1920)
events.description: Step into the shadowy world of The Cabinet of Dr. Caligari , the groundbreaking German silent horror film that forever changed the language of cinema. Presented with haunting visual design, twisted painted sets, and an atmosphere of psychological unease, this expressionist masterpiece follows the mysterious Dr. Caligari and his sleepwalking accomplice, Cesare, as a string of chilling murders terrorizes a small town. STARS: Conrad Veidt, Werner Krauss, Friedrich Feher RUNTIME: 51 Minutes GENRE: Silent Film, Film Noir, Psychological Horror, Mystery, Thriller RATING: PG-13 This show is part of the Silent Film Series , celebrating timeless scores and classic films. When the lights go down and the Mighty Wurlitzer rises from the orchestra pit, audiences are treated to a live organ performance featuring Tedde Gibson—complete with a short musical set before the credits roll and a brief introduction to each silent film. Our beloved Wurlitzer turns 100 this December, having filled the theater with music for nearly a century. The Weinberg Center , located in the heart of Downtown Frederick, MD, offers a historic backdrop for a unique film experience.

events.title: The Legend of Sleepy Hollow-Olney Theatre
events.description: Olney audiences were blown away in 2025, when we invited Synetic Theater to perform their award-winning, wordless version of Shakespeare’s A Midsummer Night’s Dream . Now they’re back, but this time they’re tackling a story with classic American roots in the intimate confines of Olney Theatre Center’s 150-seat Theatre Lab. In the haunted village of Sleepy Hollow, the past refuses to stay buried. Years after a brutal Revolutionary War encounter leaves a Hessian soldier beheaded and his beloved horse slain, the fallen rider returns as the legendary Headless Horseman—an apparition stalking the shadowed forests in search of what was taken from him. Inspired by Washington Irving’s classic tale, Sleepy Hollow reimagines the familiar legend as a haunting story of love, guilt, revenge, and redemption. Blending supernatural horror with theatrical spectacle, it asks whether the true monsters are the spirits who haunt us—or the deeds we would rather forget. By Washington Irving Adapted by Nathan Weinberger Directed by Paata Tsikurishvili Choreographed by Irina Tsikurishvili Due to the layout of the Mulitz-Gudelsky Theatre Lab, late seating is at the discretion of the House Manager. Those exiting the theatre during the performance will not be re-admitted while the performance is in progress.

events.title: Afro-Cuban All Stars
events.description: Afro-Cuban All Stars is a multigenerational orchestra devoted to promoting the full range of Cuban music, bringing together musicians across styles and eras. Led by bandleader Juan de Marcos González—also a central figure in the Buena Vista Social Club project—the ensemble reflects a long-standing approach rooted in tradition while embracing contemporary Cuban sounds. Their program moves across son, bolero, and rhythm-driven dance styles, drawing on the musical traditions of Cuba’s mid-20th-century golden age. Founded in the 1990s, the group continues to evolve through a flexible lineup that incorporates younger musicians alongside established artists. More than a fixed ensemble, Afro-Cuban All Stars operates as a shifting orchestra, adapting its sound to reflect different periods and styles, grounded in González’s concept of building on musical roots while creating space for the future.

events.title: Hermit Day
events.description: Hermit Day October 29 @ 9:30 am - 4:00 pm Day of Quiet at Bon Secours Do you… need a day of quiet and solitude to rest, reflect, be? need at least one of these each year? sense that God may be inviting you to enter silence and reorient? October 29 th might be just for you, as it is the annual celebration of National Hermit Day. Although its origins are not firmly known, many attribute Hermit Day’s origin to the 18th century and suggest a connection to the Irish Hermit Saint Colman. It gives us an opportunity to join the many others who — throughout Christian history — have entered silence and solitude to remember what is most important: to listen, to pray. A day like this has the potential to initiate or strengthen a regular practice. Since 2014, Bon Secours Retreat and Conference Center has hosted Quiet Morning events that are also opportunities for shared silence. This day will follow a similar pattern. We will begin and end together in simple prayer, have lunch in shared silence, and spend the day on our own in prayer or other quiet activities such as walking, doing art, reading, journaling — whatever you feel inclined to do. The Center’s daily Mass at 11:00 am will be available to you, if desired. This is mostly a silent retreat. Lunch is included. Guided by Joanne Cahoon.

events.description: Discover the fascinating world of superstitions, folklore, and everyday beliefs that shaped life in centuries past. On this guided tour of the William Paca House and Garden, explore the origins of customs and practices once accepted as fact and, in some cases, still observed today. From household rituals to good-luck charms and protective practices, uncover the meanings behind these enduring traditions and learn how they influenced daily life. Join us for an engaging journey into the beliefs that helped people make sense of an uncertain world and discover how echoes of these old superstitions still linger today. At the conclusion of the tour, guests are invited to enjoy seasonal refreshments and share their favorite superstition! Note: This tour will be offered on a range of dates and times in October. To see times, visit our October event calendar . Cost: $15 General Admission. $12 for Historic Annapolis members and Military. Weather or private events may alter the tour route. Please dress for the weather. Advance registration recommended; space is limited. Interested in a private version of this tour for your group of 10 or more? events.title: Making Meaning in the Modern World
events.description: Our well-being grows when we create, when we connect, and when we know that we matter to other people. Decades of research and thousands of human stories tell us that making and mattering are powerful antidotes to overwhelm and disconnection. Join New York Times bestselling authors Kelly Corrigan (The Middle Place and Tell Me More) and Jennifer Wallace (Never Enough and Mattering) for a conversation about making, mattering, and the simple things that help us build meaningful lives. Drawing from Corrigan’s exploration of creativity and making, and Wallace’s analysis and collection of research on the science of mattering, the evening weaves together personal stories and practical wisdom to explore what helps people flourish. The event features individual talks from each author and an on-stage conversation between the authors and local educators. Come celebrate the simple but powerful idea that the lives we build together are shaped by both what we make and by knowing that we matter. This event is supported by the Walton Family Foundation.

Your guide will bring to life the legends, trials, and lore that shaped our colonial past. The Witches of Maryland Pub Crawl is a 2-hour pub crawl (approx. ½ mile) into some of the storied taverns of Annapolis. Spending about 20–30 minutes at each location, you’ll relax with a cocktail while learning about the accusations, trials, and superstitions that spread through Maryland — and the lasting stories that have become part of our local history. We will visit three bars on each crawl — locations visited may include some of the following: 🍸 Drinks are not included in this tour. This tour is limited to Adults (21+) ONLY! No children. show less

events.title: The Legend of Sleepy Hollow-Olney Theatre
events.description: Olney audiences were blown away in 2025, when we invited Synetic Theater to perform their award-winning, wordless version of Shakespeare’s A Midsummer Night’s Dream . Now they’re back, but this time they’re tackling a story with classic American roots in the intimate confines of Olney Theatre Center’s 150-seat Theatre Lab. In the haunted village of Sleepy Hollow, the past refuses to stay buried. Years after a brutal Revolutionary War encounter leaves a Hessian soldier beheaded and his beloved horse slain, the fallen rider returns as the legendary Headless Horseman—an apparition stalking the shadowed forests in search of what was taken from him. Inspired by Washington Irving’s classic tale, Sleepy Hollow reimagines the familiar legend as a haunting story of love, guilt, revenge, and redemption. Blending supernatural horror with theatrical spectacle, it asks whether the true monsters are the spirits who haunt us—or the deeds we would rather forget. By Washington Irving Adapted by Nathan Weinberger Directed by Paata Tsikurishvili Choreographed by Irina Tsikurishvili Due to the layout of the Mulitz-Gudelsky Theatre Lab, late seating is at the discretion of the House Manager. events.title: The Unfinished America: A 250-Year Journey of Liberty and Economic Freedom
events.description: Meet at the World War II Kiosk and join a National Park Service volunteer for an immersive 90-minute walking tour exploring the evolution of individual liberty and economic freedom while visiting several National Mall monuments and memorials. From the towering legacy of George Washington to the revolutionary courage of the 56 Signers of the Declaration of Independence, we will trace America’s fitful yet persistent progress toward a "more perfect union." This journey weaves together iconic sites with personal stories of stowaways, soldiers, and the "Greatest Generation" to honor the sacrifices that built our modern world. As we celebrate this year's historic semiquincentennial, you are invited to connect your own family’s legacy to our shared pursuit of freedom and learn about nationwide celebrations ahead. Discover why the torch lit 250 years ago remains an exceptional beacon of democratic leadership in the world today. Memorials visited include: WWII and Washington Monument, Japanese Lantern, Martin Luther King Jr. Memorial, Korean and Vietnam War Memorials, the Lincoln Memorial, and Signers' Island.

events.title: Join Historic Annapolis: Very Superstitious! Paca House and Garden Tour: A History of Luck, Lore, and Beliefs
events.description: Discover the fascinating world of superstitions, folklore, and everyday beliefs that shaped life in centuries past. On this guided tour of the William Paca House and Garden, explore the origins of customs and practices once accepted as fact and, in some cases, still observed today. From household rituals to good-luck charms and protective practices, uncover the meanings behind these enduring traditions and learn how they influenced daily life. Join us for an engaging journey into the beliefs that helped people make sense of an uncertain world and discover how echoes of these old superstitions still linger today. At the conclusion of the tour, guests are invited to enjoy seasonal refreshments and share their favorite superstition! Note: This tour will be offered on a range of dates and times in October. To see times, visit our October event calendar . Cost: $15 General Admission. $12 for Historic Annapolis members and Military. Weather or private events may alter the tour route. Please dress for the weather. Advance registration recommended; space is limited. Interested in a private version of this tour for your group of 10 or more? Contact Cara Garside, Visitor Services Manager, at grouptours@annapolis.org . Accessibility Considerations : Accessing the interior of the William Paca House requires ascending and descending several flights of stairs. Photography Policy : Historic Annapolis reserves the right to take photographs and video footage of people of all ages at Historic Annapolis-sponsored events for publicity. If you do not wish to be photographed or filmed, please opt out by notifying Historic Annapolis staff.

events.title: Legends & Lore
events.description: Come see the darker side of Frederick. When night falls, Frederick’s familiar streets have rather different stories to tell. Climb aboard our vintage double-decker for an hour of dark tales from Frederick’s past , researched from local histories, old accounts and the legends that have lingered long after the people involved have gone. As we make our way through the city, we’ll slow down at the very places connected to these stories, from historic streets and old buildings to some of Frederick’s more famously haunted places . Along the way, you’ll hear tales of strange happenings, restless spirits and the darker chapters of local history, all told against the backdrop of Frederick after dark. And because it’s October, you’ll also get a rather good view from the top deck as the city’s historic homes and neighborhoods put on their best autumn and Halloween displays. Whether you’re a believer, a skeptic, or simply enjoy a good story with a slightly unsettling ending, Legends and Lore offers a different way to discover Frederick’s history. Just remember, it’s much easier to laugh at a ghost story when you’re not sitting on the top deck in the dark. TOUR HIGHLIGHTS Hear researched tales of Frederick’s haunted places, local legends and darker history, told where the stories happened. Experience Frederick after dark from the top deck, with historic streets, autumn displays and a few places you’ll look at rather differently afterwards. TOUR DETAILS Price: $35 per person Duration: 1 hour Recommended Age: 14+ Departure: RAK Brewing Co, 400 Sagner Ave, Frederick, MD, 21701

events.title: The Legend of Sleepy Hollow-Olney Theatre
events.description: Olney audiences were blown away in 2025, when we invited Synetic Theater to perform their award-winning, wordless version of Shakespeare’s A Midsummer Night’s Dream . Now they’re back, but this time they’re tackling a story with classic American roots in the intimate confines of Olney Theatre Center’s 150-seat Theatre Lab. In the haunted village of Sleepy Hollow, the past refuses to stay buried. Years after a brutal Revolutionary War encounter leaves a Hessian soldier beheaded and his beloved horse slain, the fallen rider returns as the legendary Headless Horseman—an apparition stalking the shadowed forests in search of what was taken from him. Inspired by Washington Irving’s classic tale, Sleepy Hollow reimagines the familiar legend as a haunting story of love, guilt, revenge, and redemption. Blending supernatural horror with theatrical spectacle, it asks whether the true monsters are the spirits who haunt us—or the deeds we would rather forget. By Washington Irving Adapted by Nathan Weinberger Directed by Paata Tsikurishvili Choreographed by Irina Tsikurishvili Due to the layout of the Mulitz-Gudelsky Theatre Lab, late seating is at the discretion of the House Manager. Those exiting the theatre during the performance will not be re-admitted while the performance is in progress.

events.title: Caroline, or Change the Musical
events.description: 8 performances | October 31 and November 6*, 7, 13, and 14 at 7:30pm | November 1, 8, and 15 at 2:00pm *Friday, November 6 will include ASL interpretation and free tickets for Montgomery County residents! Full information at www.r-m-t.org/caroline-or-change Set in one of the most pivotal times in America’s history, the Tony-nominated Caroline, or Change is riveting, moving and awe-inspiring. Featuring a virtuosic score by Jeanine Tesori (Shrek The Musical, Thoroughly Modern Millie), it blends blues, gospel and traditional Jewish melodies, creating a breathtaking medium for Kushner’s provocative and personal story. ​ In 1963, the Gellman family and their African-American maid, Caroline, live in sleepy Lake Charles, Louisiana. Caroline is drifting through life as a single mother of four working in a service job to a white family. A fragile, yet beautiful friendship develops between the young Gellman son, Noah, and Caroline. Noah’s stepmother, Rose, unable to give Caroline a raise, tells Caroline that she may keep the money that Noah leaves in his pockets. Caroline balks and refuses to take money from a child but her own children desperately need food, clothing and shoes. Outside of the laundry room, some of the greatest social advancements that the country has seen are being set in motion, and change is knocking on the door. ​ Caroline, or Change is a story that must be shared and will touch hearts. It is a story that will open minds. It is a story that will change theatergoers

events.description: Tour the most haunted building in Frederick – the National Museum of Civil War Medicine on HALLOWEEN NIGHT! Explore the building’s history amidst the darkened galleries and offices. On the tour, staff and volunteers will share stories of Civil War embalmers, the building’s most infamous tenants, and their first-hand accounts of paranormal activity that have given the building its spooky reputation. Join Historic Annapolis: Very Superstitious! Paca House and Garden Tour: A History of Luck, Lore, and Beliefs
events.description: Discover the fascinating world of superstitions, folklore, and everyday beliefs that shaped life in centuries past. On this guided tour of the William Paca House and Garden, explore the origins of customs and practices once accepted as fact and, in some cases, still observed today. From household rituals to good-luck charms and protective practices, uncover the meanings behind these enduring traditions and learn how they influenced daily life. Join us for an engaging journey into the beliefs that helped people make sense of an uncertain world and discover how echoes of these old superstitions still linger today. At the conclusion of the tour, guests are invited to enjoy seasonal refreshments and share their favorite superstition! Note: This tour will be offered on a range of dates and times in October. To see times, visit our October event calendar . Cost: $15 General Admission. $12 for Historic Annapolis members and Military. Weather or private events may alter the tour route. Please dress for the weather. Advance registration recommended; space is limited. Interested in a private version of this tour for your group of 10 or more? Contact Cara Garside, Visitor Services Manager, at grouptours@annapolis.org . Accessibility Considerations : Accessing the interior of the William Paca House requires ascending and descending several flights of stairs. Cancellation and Refund Policy : Historic Annapolis reserves the right to cancel or alter any programs. Unless otherwise stated, all tickets are non-refundable. Photography Policy : Historic Annapolis reserves the right to take photographs and video footage of people of all ages at Historic Annapolis-sponsored events for publicity. If you do not wish to be photographed or filmed, please opt out by notifying Historic Annapolis staff.
events.admission: $15 General Admission. $12 for Historic Annapolis members and Military.

events.title: Madds Buckley
events.description: In an increasingly artificial world, singer-songwriter Madds Buckley is staying undeniably human. An RIAA Gold-certified artist with more than 2 million monthly listeners, Buckley pairs clear vocals with unexpected melodies and a deep-rooted instinct for storytelling. Her music sits at a unique intersection: honest, accessible, and highly personal storytelling that often incorporates themes found in anime, video games, and narrative-driven media. Even at its most fantastical, her music never loses sight of what’s real. Following My Love Is Sick, Buckley continues to evolve with a new run of releases, including “Overboard,” “Concept Without Proof,” and “Human to You,” ahead of her forthcoming album Simple Binary and a Complex Phrase (out October 16). Expanding her sonic and thematic scope more than ever before, the album interrogates the artificial to get to the heart of what’s most real: loving, losing, and persevering through the pain. Madds Buckley has partnered with PLUS1 so that $1 per ticket goes to supporting Conscious Alliance’s mission to end hunger nationwide and feed families in need.

On this guided tour, you’ll explore the mill’s machinery, including the waterwheel, gears, and millstones that brought the process to life. events.title: Rockville Musical Theatre presents “Caroline, or Change”
events.description: 8 performances | Oct. 31 and Nov. 6*, 7, 13 & 14 at 7:30 p.m. | Nov. 1, 8 & 15 at 2 p.m. Set in one of the most pivotal times in America’s history, the Tony-nominated Caroline, or Change is riveting, moving, and awe-inspiring. Featuring a virtuosic score by Jeanine Tesori (Shrek The Musical, Thoroughly Modern Millie), it blends blues, gospel and traditional Jewish melodies, creating a breathtaking medium for Kushner’s provocative and personal story. In 1963, the Gellman family and their African-American maid, Caroline, live in sleepy Lake Charles, Louisiana. Caroline is drifting through life as a single mother of four, working in a service job for a white family. A fragile, yet beautiful friendship develops between the young Gellman son, Noah, and Caroline. Noah’s stepmother, Rose, unable to give Caroline a raise, tells Caroline that she may keep the money that Noah leaves in his pockets. Caroline balks and refuses to take money from a child, but her own children desperately need food, clothing and shoes. Outside of the laundry room, some of the greatest social advancements that the country has seen are being set in motion, and change is knocking on the door. Caroline, or Change, produces a valuable theatrical experience that continues to thrill audiences the world over. It is a story that must be shared and will touch hearts. It is a story that will open minds. It is a story that will change theatergoers for the better. Featuring one of the most powerful female roles in musi

events.description: Olney audiences were blown away in 2025, when we invited Synetic Theater to perform their award-winning, wordless version of Shakespeare’s A Midsummer Night’s Dream . Now they’re back, but this time they’re tackling a story with classic American roots in the intimate confines of Olney Theatre Center’s 150-seat Theatre Lab. In the haunted village of Sleepy Hollow, the past refuses to stay buried. Years after a brutal Revolutionary War encounter leaves a Hessian soldier beheaded and his beloved horse slain, the fallen rider returns as the legendary Headless Horseman—an apparition stalking the shadowed forests in search of what was taken from him. Inspired by Washington Irving’s classic tale, Sleepy Hollow reimagines the familiar legend as a haunting story of love, guilt, revenge, and redemption. Blending supernatural horror with theatrical spectacle, it asks whether the true monsters are the spirits who haunt us—or the deeds we would rather forget. By Washington Irving Adapted by Nathan Weinberger Directed by Paata Tsikurishvili Choreographed by Irina Tsikurishvili Due to the layout of the Mulitz-Gudelsky Theatre Lab, late seating is at the discretion of the House Manager. Those exiting the theatre during the performance will not be re-admitted while the performance is in progress.

events.description: Three DC-area acts take the stage for an evening of pop-rock energy and local legacy. The Speaks, active from 1997 to 2009, broke down barriers with anthemic music and legendary live shows, earning radio play on DC101 and selling out five consecutive 9:30 Club shows. Signed to Warner Music (Asia) in 2005, their single "High" received unprecedented worldwide airplay and remains covered by artists globally; still streamed over 1 million times monthly. Crash Boom Bang returns to the stage in 2026 after a decade away, reuniting the band that helped define DC's pop-rock chapter. They cut their teeth at Jammin' Java, packing the house show after show before touring alongside Plain White T's, Mayday Parade, and Gin Blossoms. Their 2012 EP These Wild Things earned film and TV placements, while their "V.I.P." music video surpassed 300,000 views. Produced by Tom Higgenson of Plain White T's, their debut Gold Rush set the tone for their signature anthemic hooks and high-energy sound. Now they return home for one night only. Kill For Sushi, the rebranded project of Angie Pepa and former Wandering Lies bandmates, brings a new musical direction. events.description: A Quiet Space A Silent Retreat for Rest, Reflection & Renewal Before the gatherings. Before the shopping. Before the travel. Before the expectations. Before the season asks you to give so much of yourself, give yourself a place to pause. A Quiet Space is a gentle, intentionally designed silent retreat at Harmony Hills in Deale, Maryland, created for rest, reflection, and renewal. For a few hours, step away from the noise and demands of everyday life and enter a quieter space—one where you don't have to perform, produce, solve, or explain. Simply be. Through intentional silence, reflection, stillness, and spaciousness, you'll have an opportunity to reconnect with yourself and notice what may be asking for your attention. You don't need to arrive with a particular intention. You don't need to know what you need. You don't need to have anything figured out. Just come as you are. Whether you're moving through a season of change, carrying something unseen, feeling the weight of the upcoming holidays, or simply longing for a little more quiet in your life, there is room for you here. A Quiet Space includes: • Guided moments of reflection • Periods of intentional silence • Time for personal rest and stillness • Gentle grounding practices • Space to journal, reflect, or simply be • A peaceful setting at Harmony Hills Choose the amount of quiet that feels right for you. This experience is designed with different retreat lengths so you can choose the amount of time that best meets you where you are.

events.title: African American Quilt Documentation Day in DC
events.venue: National Museum of Women in the Arts - Great Hall
events.address: 1250 New York Ave NW, Washington, DC 20005-3970
events.description: WASHINGTON, DC — The African American Quilt Documentation Study Group (AAQDSG) will host a FREE quilt documentation event in Washington, DC on Sunday, November 1, 2026, inviting the African American community to bring family quilts in to be documented, preserved, and honored as part of our shared history. Date: Sunday, November 1, 2026 Time: 10:00 AM – 4:00 PM Location: National Museum of Women in the Arts, 1250 New York Ave. NW, Washington, DC 20005 Cost: Free — pre-registration required (time slots are limited) Since the 1980s, quilt documentation has been used to preserve family legacies and record the social, cultural, and artistic significance of quilts. African American family quilts have historically been excluded from this process. Most exist today with no documented history of the quilt or its maker — what's known has been passed down orally and never recorded. "Documentation is how we hold onto that," said A'donna Richardson, Director of AAQDSG. "It's an act of honoring our ancestors, of making sure the work of the quilt maker's hands is remembered. It's a way of saying: our ancestors mattered, what they made matters, and the stories tied to their quilts matter." The process reaches beyond individual families. Documented quilts become part of the historical record that scholars, museums, and researchers rely on to understand African American creativity, survival, faith, and community. Without this work, those stories remain untold and the historical record remains misrepresented and incomplete. We are encouraging the African American community to bring their family quilts, in whatever condition (the older, the better), to the November 1 event to have them photographed and documented, and to share the stories behind them. YOU MUST REGISTER to attend: https://aaqdsg.org/events If all appointment slots are filled, send your name and contact information to afamquilydoc@aadqsg.org. Full information at www.r-m-t.org/caroline-or-change Set in one of the most pivotal times in America’s history, the Tony-nominated Caroline, or Change is riveting, moving and awe-inspiring. Featuring a virtuosic score by Jeanine Tesori (Shrek The Musical, Thoroughly Modern Millie), it blends blues, gospel and traditional Jewish melodies, creating a breathtaking medium for Kushner’s provocative and personal story. ​ In 1963, the Gellman family and their African-American maid, Caroline, live in sleepy Lake Charles, Louisiana. Caroline is drifting through life as a single mother of four working in a service job to a white family. A fragile, yet beautiful friendship develops between the young Gellman son, Noah, and Caroline. Noah’s stepmother, Rose, unable to give Caroline a raise, tells Caroline that she may keep the money that Noah leaves in his pockets. Caroline balks and refuses to take money from a child but her own children desperately need food, clothing and shoes. Outside of the laundry room, some of the greatest social advancements that the country has seen are being set in motion, and change is knocking on the door. ​ Caroline, or Change is a story that must be shared and will touch hearts. It is a story that will open minds. It is a story that will change theatergoers

events.description: October 9, 2026 – November 1, 2026 Gallery Hours: Friday-Saturday, 12-5pm; Sunday, 11am-2pm Opening Reception: Friday, October 9, 6-8pm Layered Lives: Women in Print brings together women artists from the DMV region who explore the depths of lived experience through experimental printmaking techniques. events.title: Re-Leaf Agency
events.description: A Multisensory Performance Prompting Reflection and Action Re-Leaf Agency invites you into an immersive environment of lush movement, rich sounds, provocative text, and larger-than-life video projections of trees, mushrooms, ferns, wildflowers, and streams spanning multiple surfaces. The performers summon you into the woods, amplifying all manner of small and precious flora and fauna, to reveal a needed refuge. Re-Leaf Agency is a recruitment session disguised as a performance, or maybe it’s a performance disguised as a recruitment session. Either way, this is the last time in 2026 when you can join the Agency to become a keeper of the good. Three Re-Leaf Agents - two dancers and a recruitment officer - implore you to join them in navigating the turbulent times in which we find ourselves. Amidst the anxiety of an unraveling democracy and the impacts of a changing climate, Re-Leaf Agency rekindles hope by taking the long view of the natural world. This multimedia piece is the culmination of several years documenting a sliver of earth on the edge of Maryland’s South Mountain, during which time MAD Dance director Kit Clark experienced the solace of non-human time while walking and witnessing the land. Re-Leaf Agency shares that profound experience with others. Dancers Amanda Comi and Jeanna Riscigno join Clark in this one-of-a-kind performance.

events.title: Rockville Musical Theatre presents “Caroline, or Change”
events.description: 8 performances | Oct. 31 and Nov. 6*, 7, 13 & 14 at 7:30 p.m. | Nov. 1, 8 & 15 at 2 p.m. Set in one of the most pivotal times in America’s history, the Tony-nominated Caroline, or Change is riveting, moving, and awe-inspiring. Featuring a virtuosic score by Jeanine Tesori (Shrek The Musical, Thoroughly Modern Millie), it blends blues, gospel and traditional Jewish melodies, creating a breathtaking medium for Kushner’s provocative and personal story. In 1963, the Gellman family and their African-American maid, Caroline, live in sleepy Lake Charles, Louisiana. Caroline is drifting through life as a single mother of four, working in a service job for a white family. A fragile, yet beautiful friendship develops between the young Gellman son, Noah, and Caroline. Noah’s stepmother, Rose, unable to give Caroline a raise, tells Caroline that she may keep the money that Noah leaves in his pockets. Caroline balks and refuses to take money from a child, but her own children desperately need food, clothing and shoes. Outside of the laundry room, some of the greatest social advancements that the country has seen are being set in motion, and change is knocking on the door. Caroline, or Change, produces a valuable theatrical experience that continues to thrill audiences the world over. It is a story that must be shared and will touch hearts. events.title: The Legend of Sleepy Hollow-Olney Theatre
events.description: Olney audiences were blown away in 2025, when we invited Synetic Theater to perform their award-winning, wordless version of Shakespeare’s A Midsummer Night’s Dream . Now they’re back, but this time they’re tackling a story with classic American roots in the intimate confines of Olney Theatre Center’s 150-seat Theatre Lab. In the haunted village of Sleepy Hollow, the past refuses to stay buried. Years after a brutal Revolutionary War encounter leaves a Hessian soldier beheaded and his beloved horse slain, the fallen rider returns as the legendary Headless Horseman—an apparition stalking the shadowed forests in search of what was taken from him. Inspired by Washington Irving’s classic tale, Sleepy Hollow reimagines the familiar legend as a haunting story of love, guilt, revenge, and redemption. Blending supernatural horror with theatrical spectacle, it asks whether the true monsters are the spirits who haunt us—or the deeds we would rather forget. By Washington Irving Adapted by Nathan Weinberger Directed by Paata Tsikurishvili Choreographed by Irina Tsikurishvili Due to the layout of the Mulitz-Gudelsky Theatre Lab, late seating is at the discretion of the House Manager. Those exiting the theatre during the performance will not be re-admitted while the performance is in progress.

events.title: The Nth Power
events.description: The Nth Power, featuring guitarist Nick Cassarino, bassist Nate Edgar, and drummer Nikki Glaspie, believes in the healing power of music. The seasoned trio delivers a transcendent blend of soul, funk, rock, and rhythm and blues anchored by multi-part vocal harmonies and elevated musicianship that inspires audiences to dance, groove, or stand transfixed. Aligning in New Orleans during Jazz Fest, The Nth Power's electric live performances have floored audiences ever since. Following their breakout 2013 EP Basic Minimum Skills Test, the band released two acclaimed studio albums and two live albums, earning national coverage in Relix, Modern Drummer, Glide, Paste, and Sirius XM Radio. Their individual credentials include collaborations with Beyoncé, Snarky Puppy, Maceo Parker, Dumpstaphunk, and John Brown's Body. "It's my dream team," said bandleader Glaspie. "Each one of us is a songwriter, so when we get together, everything becomes that much stronger." Their inspirational sets have floored audiences at Electric Forest, High Sierra, Peachfest, North Coast Music Festival, and Hulaween. Maintaining New Orleans as their spiritual home, the celebratory essence of that city's music culture is palpable in each performance. Something magical is happening in this band. Jammin' Java welcomes The Nth Power to near Fairfax County, Virginia.

events.description: FORBIDDEN: Godfathers in the Bay Area metal scene, Forbidden have returned with their first album in 16 years to unleash 12 fierce, uncompromising, and supremely progressive songs which signal an almighty return. Conceived by founder and guitarist Craig Locicero alongside his creative brother, drummer Chris Kontos, the foundational energy of bassist Matt Camacho, the versatility and poise of guitarist Jeremy Von Epp, and Skinner’s voracious fresh approach, Forbidden sees the band arriving at their finest hour with their richest-ever line-up. With Skinner stepping up to take on lyrical duties, Forbidden takes a fierce and uncompromising look into the eyes of our times without taking sides, instead imploring people to recognize the false conflicts created by the current society and how they can conquer and rise above them. In addition, Forbidden pay homage to classic American heavy metal band Savatage in the shape of a malevolent and mesmeric cover of “Sirens”, which embraces Greek mythology. Arts on Stage Presents...A More Perfect Union
events.description: Arts on Stage Presents… A More Perfect Union Wednesday, November 4, 2026 in the Hammonds Lane Theatre 10:15 am 12 pm $11.50 Grades 3-8 Study guide, click here A spirited folk musical introducing the people and events that led to the writing and signing of our Constitution. The story of “A More Perfect Union” begins in Boston, 1773 and ends at the Constitutional Convention in Philadelphia, 1787. The play covers the critical and tempestuous time in our nation’s history in which revolution, war, and a failed attempt at self-governing finally led to the writing of the U.S. Constitution and the birth of our country as we know it today. Briefly addressing the American Revolution and the underlying causes thereof, the majority of the play examines that period between the winning of our Independence and the formation of our national government.

events.title: Sophia Bush
events.description: Sophia Bush has always understood the power of stories. She’s seen it in the connection millions of viewers have had to the women she’s played on-screen—Dr. Sam Griffith on “Good Sam” and Dr. Cass Beckman on “Grey’s Anatomy,” Detective Erin Lindsay on “Chicago P.D.,” and the iconic Brooke Davis on “One Tree Hill.” She’s seen it in her activism, where speaking truth to inequality and power has prompted real change. And she’s seen it in her personal life, when her experiences and opinions have been distorted to drive clicks and create drama. In And I Will Tell You Mine, Bush shares stories about what has most shaped her: her childhood in Los Angeles, the unexpected road from journalism student to actor, navigating Hollywood and fighting for her character’s integrity, and the realities of marriage and divorce. She also offers sides of herself not often seen: the lifelong learner, the friend, the adventurer. And I Will Tell You Mine is an account of becoming, un-becoming, and becoming again to return home to our truest selves. events.description: Go beyond King Street on a 90-minute guided walk through Alexandria's remarkable Wilkes Street Cemetery Complex—13 historic cemeteries, 52 acres, and more than 35,000 burials in one walkable landscape. Led by independent historian and cemetery superintendent David Heiby, creator of Gravestone Stories, the tour connects Alexandria's past to the American Revolution, War of 1812, Civil War, Cold War, and more. Meet George Washington's pallbearers, Revolutionary War patriots, Civil War soldiers, a Soviet spy, and others whose stories illuminate more than two centuries of Alexandria history. Every stop is grounded in original research, cemetery records, and discoveries made within the complex, including graves rediscovered after nearly 200 years. Tours are limited to small groups. The 90-minute walk covers approximately 1 to 1.5 miles over historic cemetery paths and uneven terrain. Free parking is available. Tours are offered Fridays and Saturdays at 1:00 p.m., with an additional Thursday tour at 3:30 p.m. Tickets are $30 per person and include the official Gravestone Stories companion e-book. See the Gravestone Stories website for current availability and booking.

events.description: Experiencing history through outdoor mindfulness at Woodlawn & Pope-Leighey House. About the Session: The sessions are approximately 90-minutes long and are conducted in relative silence. They include warm-ups, centering, and breathing exercises to connect participants to their bodies and the world around them. These are followed by a walk and an extended sit which encourages participants to become more fully open and present to their surroundings. We conclude with a returning ritual and a chance to reflect on the experience. This time in nature will not be strenuous; most abilities can be accommodated. All ages are welcomed but children under 16 must be accompanied by an adult. Important Arrival & Check-In Details Check-In Location: All participants must check in at Woodlawn, regardless of session topic. Timing: Sessions start promptly at 12:00 PM (Sundays). Please arrive early to ensure a timely start. Duration: Approximately 90 minutes. Fall Schedule & Locations Sunday, October 11 | Woodlawn Sunday, October 25 | Pope-Leighey House Sunday, November 1 | Woodlawn Sunday, November 8 | Pope-Leighey House Tickets & Policies Price: $30 per ticket. All purchases directly support the preservation of this historic site. Weather: Programs take place rain or shine.

The hike is weather permitting, and make sure to bring appropriate footwear and clothing for the climate.

events.description: Immerse yourself in the daily life of soldiers, military officers, and the camp followers who traveled with the army as you explore a Revolutionary War encampment. At this hands-on attraction, you can touch the items inside the soldiers' tents and officer's tent, wash clothes in the laundry yard, and examine cooking utensils used by camp followers. See two daily programs about enlisting in General Washington's army and how soldiers prepared their meals while traveling. This attraction is made possible thanks to Americana Corner.
